text: Currently, 80 percent of NH is commercial grade and used in agriculture. For pipelined, stored, and transported NH , 3 3 the water content is important; a water content in NH of 0.2–0.5 percent improves safety due 3 to a lower risk of stress corrosion cracking. Since NH absorbs water easily, this impurity is 3 expensive and energy-intensive to remove. Furthermore, ammonia industry experts that are a part of the Ammonia Energy Association have come together to promote a “future fuel standard” for ammonia. Airgas, an industrial supplier, suggests a fuel-grade ammonia to have 99.5 wt% purity and a minimum water content of 0.2 wt% (Richardson, 2020). MAN Energy Solutions, a manufacturer of engines and machinery for maritime applications, has proposed a fuel standard for ammonia as a marine fuel, which aligns closely to commercial-grade ammonia (Jacobsen, 2020). Per the Electric Power Research Institute, ammonia, even with 2 wt% water content, could be burned as fuel for power generation (Atchison, 2020). The use of commercial-grade ammonia has also been demonstrated in fuel cells and cracking applications (Atchison, 2020). 19 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION To best match current and future demands for ammonia, the plant was designed with the goal of achieving a commercial-grade ammonia product at 99.5 wt% purity. The options range from liquid ammonia storage at ambient temperature and elevated pressures to storage at ambient pressure and low temperatures, and each storage option has tradeoffs. The atmospheric insulated cylindrical tank was selected for ammonia storage because it is advantageous for storing large quantities of NH , it is likely to be the cheapest storage option, 3 and it is the option most relevant for an end use related to storing NH at ship or pipeline 3 loading and unloading points.
